model: SQL Server 2022 Developer Edition (64-bit) on Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS), standalone

capture.setup: docker run --name fxlab-d-mssql --hostname mssql-lab -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e MSSQL_PID=Developer mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest; sqlcmd as sa: databases Inventory (FULL recovery, 5000 rows) and Payroll (SIMPLE recovery); discovery login openmap (SQL authentication) with VIEW SERVER STATE, VIEW ANY DEFINITION, VIEW ANY DATABASE and a user in master.
capture.command: Recording TCP proxy (lab-only Go program inside apps/collectors, removed after capture) between the OpenMap database collector's real prober (Collector.Collect from the Windows host, engine option set, port = proxy) and the container's 127.0.0.1-published port; every byte each side sent is stored in order, one file per TCP connection, with wire.json indexing the direction, offset and length of each contiguous segment. Target 127.0.0.1:41433 (mssql-lab), login openmap, encrypt=disable: the driver offers ENCRYPT_NOT_SUP in PRELOGIN and the server (default, encryption not forced) answers without TLS, so LOGIN7 and every query travel in clear TDS and can be replayed.

files.name: wire.json
files.description: Index of the recorded conversation: per connection, ordered client/server segments (offset, length) into the .bin file

files.name: wire/conn-1.bin
files.description: Raw TCP bytes of connection 1 exactly as exchanged (client and server segments concatenated in order)

redactions.what: LOGIN7 HostName (Windows workstation name of the capture machine, 6 UCS-2 characters at byte offset 238)
LOGIN7 Password (obfuscated lab password, 28 bytes at byte offset 264)
LOGIN7 ClientID (MAC address of the capture machine, 6 bytes at byte offset 216)
